audiences.executive: Use the public cloud for what it does best (leaving a data centre, a disaster, a peak) without rewriting applications or retraining teams.
audiences.technical: The same platform and operations in the data centre and in the cloud; machines move without new addresses; one set of policies.
audiences.financial: Spend existing cloud commitments, rent capacity while hardware is late or scarce, and keep a small standing footprint that grows only when needed.

people: The owner of the cloud strategy and its commitments
The cloud platform or landing-zone team
Finance, for commitments and reserved pricing
Licensing, for software counted per core

objections.says: Our strategy is cloud native: we will rewrite the applications.
objections.clarify: Which applications, by when, and what runs until then?
objections.answer: Move first without rewriting, then modernise the ones worth it at their own pace, in the same place.
objections.prove: Move a test application as it is and run it in the cloud with its current tools.

objections.says: Running our own platform in the cloud costs more than native services.
objections.clarify: Compared on which price, on demand or reserved, and with which licences counted per core?
objections.answer: Compare the total for the same footprint, with reserved pricing, existing commitments and per-core licences included.
objections.prove: Cost the test footprint on demand and reserved, licences included, beside the native estimate.

objections.says: We are waiting for new hardware anyway.
objections.clarify: When will it arrive, and what is blocked until then?
objections.answer: Run what is on hold in the cloud now, on the same platform, and decide whether it comes back once the servers arrive.
objections.prove: Deploy a cloud cluster and run a blocked workload on it within the test window.

objections.says: Our data must stay in the country.
objections.clarify: Which data, under which rule, and does it cover backups and logs?
objections.answer: Choose the region or sovereign cloud by the rule, and show where every copy lives.
objections.prove: Show where every copy of a test dataset lives, backups included, and that nothing leaves the region.
